title: Jeers
paragraphs: “Naofumi, the way you’re saying that… it’s basically just a threat.”
“Yeah, I am threatening him… but I figured it was still too early for him to actually listen.”
Quickly wrapping up his exchange with Ren, Father seemed to realize that the dragon could understand him, so he pressed further.
“Uh… I think you already know this, but the fact that I have you pinned down means you’re losing this fight. And the people behind me—any one of them is strong enough to defeat you alone.”

This was one of Father’s negotiation tactics: intimidation. He once told me that when an opponent refuses to talk, this is the best way to force them to listen. And sure enough, the rival momentarily froze at Father’s words. However—
“Gyaooooo!”
He roared as if to say, I don’t care! How foolish.
Looks like it’s finally my turn, isn’t it? I tightened my grip on my spear, focusing my power.
“Why are you looking at me with those sparkling eyes? Whatever you’re thinking, Motoyasu, I’m not doing it.”
“Oh, is that so? What a shame.”
“Motoyasu, why are you even here…?”
“Are you sure you’re not just trying to kill this dragon?”
What? Weren’t we supposed to recruit him by force? As for killing the dragon… Honestly, I couldn’t care less either way. If I had to say, I suppose I was indifferent.
…But maybe I should eliminate this rival trying to win Father’s favor?
“Something about this feels off, but let’s keep going… If he won’t listen, we’ll have to lure him in with bait.”
Father turned to Ren.
“Ren, give me the dragon core stones!”
“Got it.”
Ren tossed Father a large sack filled with core stones from dragons we’d defeated earlier. Father held up the sack, making sure the rival saw it.
“I’ve heard you’re the weaker Dragon Emperor. If you accept these core stones, how about listening to what we have to say? I promise, it won’t be a bad deal for you!”
“Gyaoooooo!”
The rival spewed fire directly at Father. But he didn’t even bother defending himself. The flames flowed over him, passing through as if he were nothing more than a swaying willow leaf.
“Gyao!?”
The shock on the rival’s face was unmistakable. And there stood Father, completely unscathed.
“Do you get it now? You can’t even hurt us. So please… just hear us out.”
The rival, as if admitting defeat, lowered his head and lost his will to fight.
“That was a close one.”
“Yes. I understand how high Naofumi-san’s defense is, but even so, I thought that was dangerous.”
“Yeah… but as expected of the Shield Hero. That dragon’s breath attack curved around him…”
Sakura-chan and the others were still trying to charge in, but now that I saw the negotiation had succeeded, I relaxed.
“…So, what do you want with me?”
With a sigh of resignation, the rival finally spoke. Sensing his loss of fighting spirit, the surrounding monsters quickly fled the scene.
“Honestly… what could possibly make you think negotiating with me was a good idea?”

“Well, we’ve got a lot of circumstances on our side, but let’s start with the main reason. There’s a powerful Dragon Emperor in Faubrey, and he’s our enemy. We’re going to take him down, and in exchange for a piece of him… we want your help.”
“Oh? Quite a generous offer. That is, if you can actually defeat him.”
“We’re the Four Holy Heroes. And we’re strong enough that the battle itself won’t take long.”
“I cannot determine if you are trustworthy. But if I refuse, what happens to me?”
“Well… ideally, we’d like your help. But if you refuse, we’ll just use these core stones to raise a new dragon and persuade them instead.”
Either way, it had to be done. Honestly, it didn’t have to be him. Any dragon would do.
“It’s just that our previous rival asked us to prioritize you, so we did.”
“That’s right! Be grateful for Motoyasu-sama’s kindness and Naofumi-sama’s generosity!”
“Yeah, yeah! If you won’t join us, then get out!”
“Get out!”
“Get out, desu wa!”
At this point, I and the Filolials unleashed a relentless heckling barrage. Together, we chanted, demanding he leave.
“Ugh… how annoying…”
“I wonder whose fault it is that we ended up here in the first place?”
“Um… let’s just ignore them for now, please.”
Father directed that last part at the rival.
But we weren’t ignoring it at all!
“Hmph… To be rejected by these Filolials only makes me all the more obligated to join this discussion.”
“He sounds so grandiose, but he acts so childish.”
“Yeah. That deep, weighty voice doesn’t match the way he talks at all.”
Ren and Itsuki joined in, offering their own jabs. We doubled down on our Get out! chants.
“…They say if a deal sounds too good, there’s usually a catch. But fine, I’ll listen.”
“Well, that’s a start. Now, where should I begin…? Right. Let’s go over why we came here and why we want to convince you. First—”

Father began explaining to the rival. Starting with how I was stuck in a time loop, how I gained Ren and Itsuki’s trust, and how I helped Father. Then, he laid out the events of the previous loop—everything I had told him.
“So, Motoyasu-kun calls her ‘assistant,’ but apparently, you have a demi-human girl as your adopted daughter. It seems that in the previous loop, I was the one who took her in.”
“Hmm, I could dismiss that as a fabricated story.”
“Yeah, I figured. It’d be hard to present definitive proof.”
It’s difficult to prove something that comes from the future. I also try to think if there’s any key information that might help persuade this rival.
“That said… serving under the Four Holy Heroes is something worth considering. Even if the terms are questionable.”
“I can guarantee that you’ll grow stronger. At the very least, I want you to trust us based on mutual benefit.”
The rival glances at Yuki-chan and the others. He does have a strong desire for power, after all.

“Hmm… very well. Then I shall also take some precautionary measures of my own. As a condition for accepting your offer, I require several of the core stones you planned to give me. I have no intention of deceiving you.”
“Huh? Oh, okay.”
Father takes out the core stones and hands them over to the rival. A few of the stones float into the air before the rival consumes them. It looks like his power increased slightly.
“An advance payment, then… Very well, follow me.”

With that, the rival leads us toward his den. In front of the den, his subordinates—or perhaps his wives?—seem to be going about their daily lives. We stop a short distance away and watch as the rival returns to his den. The rival communicates with the other monsters through a series of cries. Among them is the assistant. She has the same pure expression as when she spoke with Father earlier. She’s snuggled up to one of the monsters, gently cradling an egg in her arms.
“Welcome back, Father!”
“Hmm… Have you been behaving?”
“Yeah! Just now, the egg twitched a little!”
“Oh. I hope it hatches soon.”
“I wonder what kind of baby will come out? A little brother? A little sister? I can’t wait!”
She looks so happy. The rival, too, seems to smile at the sight, as if he finds it heartwarming.
“Now then, Windia, I have something to talk to you about.”
“What is it?”
The assistant tilts her head as the rival hesitates to speak.
“Well… how should I put this… Windia, this is a rather harsh truth, but… as you probably already know, you are not my biological child.”
The assistant lowers her head.
“…Yeah. And?”
“That being said… I believe the time has come for you to leave my nest.”
The assistant looks up at the rival, her eyes welling with tears. Meanwhile, the rival glances toward our hiding spot several times, as if fidgeting. He seems uneasy.
“I kept postponing it, waiting for the right time. I thought I’d wait until you were a bit older… Windia, you are still very young.”
“…Father?”
“But the older you grow, the harder it will be for you to return to human society.”
“Then make me your wife!”
With an innocent smile, the assistant declares this to the rival.
Huh? The rival seems to recoil, his face turning red.
Aha! He’s a complete doting parent. No wonder he keeps getting killed by Ren in every loop.
“This is getting weird. I feel like I’m watching some embarrassing romantic moment, like a side character peeking at the protagonist’s first date in a dating sim.”
“What kind of extreme analogy is that…? Well, he does seem like the cowardly dragon Motoyasu described.”
“Yeah, and he’s not that strong either.”
“Dragons have their own lives, I suppose… but seeing this moment, it does feel kind of heartwarming.”
We each whisper our own impressions from our hiding spot. Ah, Yuki-chan and the others are waiting further back. We don’t want to get noticed, after all.
